All numbers from the script's output (full JSON at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-harshodaikolluru-Public-askmukthiguru-8119b0e8/b0a8ecf7-4510-49f5-8408-71d71a89e3ca/scratchpad/regex-scan/out.json). Scope: backend/ and scripts/ minus .venv, venv, node_modules, __pycache__, tests, test_*.py, conftest.py, and a few scratch dirs (.work, .hypothesis, scratch, .claude).

TOTALS: 1558 call sites = 1434 literal-resolved + 124 unresolved (36 of those are f-strings; 88 are other dynamic expressions). 317 files; 992 distinct literal patterns. By function: compile 679, sub 317, search 190, findall 126, split 58, match 37, fullmatch 17, finditer 10. Constant resolution covers module-level string constants, string concatenation, and loops over module-level string lists; it does not cover patterns built in other functions.

DUPLICATES: 180 pattern strings appear in more than one file. Collapsing the 100 byte-identical scripts/ops mirrors leaves 97 real cross-file duplicates. Most are trivial (\\s+, \\w+). The only substantive ones are the 7x <think>.*?</think> and the 5+ YouTube-id regexes, which are shared-helper candidates.

INLINE CALLS (item 3): 694 re.search/match/sub/findall/split/fullmatch/finditer calls with a literal pattern inside a function (recompiled or re's internal 512-entry cache lookup each call), 325 of them under serve dirs (backend/app, rag, services, guardrails, routers, domain, memory). Heaviest files: rag/nodes/generation.py 44, services/quote_weaver.py 16, services/okf/wiki_dreamer.py 16, services/first_person_evidence_policy.py 12, rag/nodes/utils.py 11, services/lettuce_detect_service.py 9, services/memory/okf_store.py 9. A further 19 re.compile calls sit inside functions (14 in serve dirs). Caveat: 'serve dirs' is path-based, not call-graph-based, so some of the 325 are on the dormant generation lane or offline tools such as wiki_dreamer, not on the live first-person path. Python's re cache makes the per-call cost small. This is a hygiene and consistency issue, not a measured latency problem. I did not time it.

REDOS: 31 heuristic candidates (nested quantifier, adjacent overlapping unbounded quantifiers, or overlapping alternation inside a repeat) were timed with 258 subprocess runs at lengths 5,000 and 50,000 with a 5 s kill. 4 exceeded 0.2 s, listed above. Only one is reachable from user-controlled input: first_person_bridge.py:124 _COMPOUND_QUESTION_RE, applied to the chat query (1095), with the chat input cap at 10,000 chars. It is quadratic (2.7 s at 5k, so roughly 11 s at 10k by extrapolation; 10k was not measured). Recommend a bounded rewrite or a length guard before calling it. The other 3 slow patterns run only on corpus/OKF/LLM-output text. The adversarial inputs are heuristic and the scan is not exhaustive: other patterns could be slow on inputs the generator did not try, and the 27 candidates under 0.2 s are not proven safe. Not checked: whether any existing OUTSTANDING_ISSUES or task-list ID covers regex performance. A grep for 'regex|ReDoS' found only A12 (crisis regex convergence) and A20 (rejected clip-text regex repair), neither related, so already_registered is empty for all findings.

Scan limits: analysis uses Python 3.12 re._parser on the backend venv; flags are read from literal re.X args only; unresolved f-string patterns were counted but not analysed.
